summary: Bary-Soroker, Koukoulopoulos and Kozma prove that a random monic integer polynomial of degree n, with independent coefficients drawn from a fixed finitely supported law μ and non-zero constant term, has no divisor of positive degree ≤ θ(μ)n with probability 1 − O(n^{−c}) (Theorem 2), and is irreducible with Galois group A_n or S_n with that probability under Fourier conditions modulo four primes: for N ≥ 35 consecutive coefficients (Theorem 1(a)), laws with small ℓ²-norm (Theorem 3, Corollary 1(b)), odd powers (Theorem 4) and random sets (Theorem 5); for 2 to 34 consecutive values and arithmetic progressions it is irreducible with positive probability (Theorem 1(b), Theorem 3.5). The engine is joint equidistribution of the reductions modulo four primes in 𝔽_p[T] beyond the square-root barrier (Proposition 2.3), the anatomy of polynomials over 𝔽_p with a Brun sieve (Proposition 2.2), Konyagin's small-factor argument (Proposition 2.1) and a Łuczak–Pyber theorem for random partitions with a ramified Frobenius (Propositions 2.4 and 12.1). The atlas plans prime counting, sieves, finite-field character sums and Mahler measure, and Tau Ceti has polynomial Galois groups with Frobenius elements; none has random polynomials of growing degree. 133 items (15 library, 3 planned, 115 missing) are routed to Part IIs of ArithmeticStatistics (random polynomials) and of Tau Ceti's PolynomialGaloisGroups (ramified merging and random partitions) and to five source routes. Twenty-five mistakes are recorded. Among them are a lost negation in Theorem 7, a missing four-prime hypothesis in Theorem 8, an unproved exponent in Theorem 2 and false Hölder comparisons in Remark 2.2. The gaps in Lemmas 3.7 and 12.9 and in the height range of Theorem 4 are repaired.

items.name: Monic fixed-degree polynomial family
items.statement: M(n)={A∈ℤ[T]: A monic, deg A=n}, with n∈ℕ; M_p(n) is the analogous family over 𝔽_p for prime p. M(0)={1}.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.1.api1
api.statement: Construct T^n+Σ_{j<n}a_jT^j from n coefficients.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.1.api2
api.statement: Coefficients below n recover the input; coefficient n=1 and coefficients above n vanish.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.1.api3
api.statement: Coefficientwise reduction preserves monicity and degree.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Independent coefficient product law
items.statement: For probability masses μ_0,…,μ_{n−1} on ℤ, PM(n)(A)=∏_{j<n}μ_j(coeff_j A) on M(n). Independence is across coefficient positions, not across reductions at different primes; identical distribution is not assumed.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.2.api1
api.statement: Push the finite product measure along the coefficient equivalence.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.2.api2
api.statement: Probability of a coefficient cylinder is the product of the specified masses.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.2.api3
api.statement: Transport polynomial events to coefficient vectors; sum of all masses is 1.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Conditioning on nonzero constant coefficient
items.statement: For a discrete probability law p and event E of positive mass, p(·|E)=1_E p/p(E); here E={a_0≠0}. PMF.filter implements the generic normalization, and the polynomial specialization changes only μ_0.
items.locator: arXiv v3, §1 (1.2), p. 3; proof Theorem 7 p. 14
items.note: Generic normalized carrier is present; product-law identification is a proposed integration lemma, not attributed to PMF.filter.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.3.api1
api.statement: Apply PMF.filter with a support witness in E.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.3.api2
api.statement: For a∈E, conditioned mass equals p(a)/p(E); outside E it is zero.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.3.api3
api.statement: Identify the polynomial conditional law with product law using μ_0(·|a_0≠0).

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Uniform nonzero-constant coefficient family
items.statement: For finite N⊂ℤ with |N|≥2 and n≥1, Υ_N(n) consists of monic degree-n polynomials whose n nonleading coefficients lie in N and whose constant coefficient is nonzero; equip it with uniform probability. Its cardinality is |N\{0}|·|N|^(n−1).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.4.api1
api.statement: Build the finite family from a nonzero constant choice and n−1 unrestricted choices.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.4.api2
api.statement: Uniform Υ equals iid uniform-on-N law conditioned on a_0≠0.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.4.api3
api.statement: Translate event probability into count divided by |N\{0}|·|N|^(n−1).

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Coefficient concentration norms
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.5.api1
api.statement: Define the norm using counting measure, not a probability measure on ℤ.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.5.api2
api.statement: For a uniform N-element set, ||μ||_2²=||μ||_∞=1/N.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.5.api3
api.statement: Expose ||μ||_∞<1 iff μ is not a point mass.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Joint reduction at several primes
items.statement: For a finite set ℙ of distinct primes, P=∏p∈ℙ p. Reduce a single A∼PM(n) coefficientwise to A_ℙ=(A mod p)_p in ∏M_p(n); its law is the pushforward of PM(n). It need not equal a product of its marginals.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.6.api1
api.statement: Construct the joint reduction as one measurable map.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.6.api2
api.statement: Marginal reduction at ℚ⊂ℙ is the pushforward under coordinate projection.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.6.api3
api.statement: Uniform coefficients mod P give a product of uniform reductions via CRT.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Vector polynomial ring, divisibility and norm
items.statement: For finite ℙ, 𝔽_ℙ[T]=∏_{p∈ℙ}𝔽_p[T]. For a tuple D of monic polynomials, ||D||_ℙ=∏p p^(deg D_p); divisibility, gcd, lcm and congruence are coordinatewise. M_ℙ(ℓ)=∏M_p(ℓ_p).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.7.api1
api.statement: Use the product of polynomial rings, with monicity imposed in each coordinate.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.7.api2
api.statement: ||DE||=||D||·||E|| on monic tuples.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.7.api3
api.statement: The quotient modulo D has ||D|| residue classes.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Fourier transform of an integer probability mass
items.statement: μhat(θ)=Σ_{a∈ℤ}μ(a)exp(2πiaθ), for θ∈ℝ/ℤ. The series converges absolutely, μhat(0)=1 and |μhat(θ)|≤1.
items.note: Missing item is the Z-PMF normalized-frequency adapter used by this paper, not a plan to reconstruct generic characteristic functions. PM.0's reviewed audit explicitly marks generic characteristic functions built.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.8.api1
api.statement: Define the absolutely convergent sum as a periodic function.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.8.api2
api.statement: Translation of μ by b multiplies μhat(θ) by exp(2πibθ).

api.name: RandomPolynomial.8.api3
api.statement: Reduction modulo q gives the same transform at frequencies k/q.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Coset Fourier control
items.statement: For P>1 squarefree, s>0 and real γ, α(s,γ;P)=max_{QR=P,Q>1,ℓ mod R} Q^(γ−1)Σ_{k mod Q}|μhat(k/Q+ℓ/R)|^s. Write α(P)=α(1,1/2;P).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.9.api1
api.statement: Compute all divisors Q>1 and shifted frequency cosets.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.9.api2
api.statement: α(P)≤(min_{p|P}p)^(-1/2)Σ_{k mod P}|μhat(k/P)|.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.9.api3
api.statement: A strict bound α<1 supplies the n-dependent margin for all sufficiently large n.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Fourier product σ
items.statement: For X∈∏𝔽_p((1/T)), σ_ℙ(n;X)=∏_{j=0}^{n−1}|μhat_j(ψ_ℙ(T^jX))|, where ψ is item 13. This is the modulus of the characteristic function of the random polynomial pairing.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.10.api1
api.statement: Build the finite product with each coefficient's own μ_j.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.10.api2
api.statement: 0≤σ≤1; n=0 gives 1.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.10.api3
api.statement: Dropping factors gives an upper bound, used to remove j=0.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Joint congruence discrepancy Δ
items.statement: For real m≥0, Δ_ℙ(n;m)=Σ_{D_p monic,deg D_p≤m,T∤D_p ∀p} max_{C mod D}|P(A_ℙ≡C mod D)−1/||D||_ℙ|. All maxima and sums are finite; m is truncated by integer degrees.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.11.api1
api.statement: Expose the maximum over all residue classes, including the zero class.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.11.api2
api.statement: Δ is monotone in m and dominates the one-prime marginal discrepancy.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.11.api3
api.statement: Uniform independent reduction coefficients give zero discrepancy when every degree bound is ≤n.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Reduced-fraction discrepancy δ
items.statement: For ℓ_p≥0 integers, δ_ℙ(n;ℓ)=(∏p p^(ℓ_p))^(-1)Σ_{H∈M_ℙ(ℓ),T∤H_p}Σ_{G mod H,(G_p,H_p)=1 ∀p}σ_ℙ(n;G/H).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.12.api1
api.statement: Construct the reduced residue sum with componentwise coprimality.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.12.api2
api.statement: For ℓ=0, use the unique residue class mod 1 and δ=1.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.12.api3
api.statement: Reindex G by multiplication by T^a because T∤H.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Laurent residue character
items.statement: In 𝔽_p((1/T)), res X is the coefficient of T^(−1). Let ψ_p(X)=res X/p mod 1, and ψ_ℙ(X)=Σ_pψ_p(X_p)∈ℝ/ℤ. Implement using LaurentSeries with variable U=1/T and res=coefficient of U¹; the character depends on this variable reversal.
items.note: Mathlib LaurentSeries supplies the carrier, but the reversed-variable residue/character integration is missing; not a new Laurent-series theory.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.13.api1
api.statement: Project the Laurent coefficient and compose with the canonical additive character.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.13.api2
api.statement: ψ is additive and is zero on polynomial tuples.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.13.api3
api.statement: Distinct-prime denominators imply ψ_ℙ(X)=0 iff every residue coefficient is 0.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Negative-power torus and normalized Haar law
items.statement: T_p={Σ_{j≤−1}c_jT^j} as an additive compact group, with Haar probability dX_p. Every Laurent series Y has unique decomposition A+X with A∈𝔽_p[T],X∈T_p; ||Y||_T=p^max{j<0:c_j≠0}, or 0 if X=0. T_ℙ and its law are finite products.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.14.api1
api.statement: Construct the additive compact group and normalized Haar measure; do not claim a unital subring.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.14.api2
api.statement: Extract polynomial and negative-power parts with unique reconstruction.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.14.api3
api.statement: A ball ||X||_T<p^(−m) has mass p^(−m), fixing the first m coefficients to 0.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Monic reduced polynomial fractions
items.statement: For ℓ≥0, reduced fractions are G/H with H monic of degree ℓ, deg G<ℓ and gcd(G,H)=1, regarded in 𝔽_p((1/T)). For ℓ=0 the sole representative is 0/1. Require T∤H only when using T-shift reindexing.
items.locator: arXiv v3, §4 p. 30; Remark 6.1 and Lemma 6.2 pp. 32–33
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.15.api1
api.statement: Choose canonical reduced numerator and monic denominator.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.15.api2
api.statement: Different reduced fractions of denominator degree ℓ have fractional distance≥p^(−2ℓ).

api.name: RandomPolynomial.15.api3
api.statement: For A/B=Q+R/B with R≠0, ||A/B||_T=p^(deg R−deg B).

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Nonconstant divisor event
items.statement: For monic A of degree n and real b, Bad_b(A) means ∃monic D∈ℤ[T], D|A and 1≤deg D≤b. Unit divisors are excluded. For n≥2, A reducible over ℚ iff Bad_{n/2}(A), by Gauss's lemma and factor-degree additivity.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.16.api1
api.statement: Expose the witness D with positive degree.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.16.api2
api.statement: For b<1 the event is empty.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.16.api3
api.statement: Pass an integral monic factor to factors of identical degree modulo every prime.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Pointwise Fourier decay
items.statement: If |μhat_j(k/P)|≤β∈[0,1] for all P∤k and 1≤j<n, and every fraction G_p/H_p is reduced with T∤H_p, then for any q∈ℙ with ℓ_q=deg H_q≥1, σ_ℙ(n;G/H)≤β^floor((n−1)/ℓ_q).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Characteristic function factorization
items.statement: For every X∈𝔽_ℙ((1/T)), E exp(2πiψ_ℙ(AX))=exp(2πiψ_ℙ(T^nX))∏_{j<n}μhat_j(ψ_ℙ(T^jX)).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Fourier reduction of congruence discrepancy
items.statement: For m≥0 and r=|ℙ|, Δ_ℙ(n;m)≤(floor(m)+1)^r Σ_{0≤ℓ_p≤m,max ℓ_p≥1}δ_ℙ(n;ℓ).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Torus character orthogonality
items.statement: For A∈𝔽_ℙ[T], ∫_{T_ℙ}exp(2πiψ_ℙ(AX))dX=1 if A=0 and 0 otherwise.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Haar finite-coordinate product identity
items.statement: For m≥0 and functions f_0,…,f_{m−1}:ℝ/ℤ→ℂ, ∫_{T_p}∏_{j<m}f_j(ψ_p(T^jX))dX=p^(−m)∏_{j<m}Σ_{ξ mod p}f_j(ξ/p).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Polynomial Farey large-sieve inequality
items.statement: For nonnegative f_0,…,f_{m−1} on ℝ/ℤ and integer ℓ≥m/2, Σ_{H monic,deg H=ℓ}Σ_{G mod H,(G,H)=1}∏_{j<m}f_j(ψ_p(T^jG/H))≤p^(2ℓ−m)∏_{j<m}Σ_{ξ mod p}f_j(ξ/p).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Iterated Fourier L1 estimate
items.statement: Let s≥1 integer, α≥0, γ≥1/2 and suppose Σ_{k mod Q}|μhat_j(k/Q+ℓ/R)|^s≤αQ^(1−γ) for every 1≤j<n,QR=P,Q>1,ℓ. If L=max_pℓ_p and m=floor((n−1)/s), then δ_ℙ(n;ℓ)≤P^max(0,L−γm) α^min(2L,m).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Approximate joint equidistribution
items.statement: For r distinct primes with product P, n≥P^4, γ≥1/2, integer 1≤s≤n^(1/100), suppose Σ_{k mod Q}|μhat_j(k/Q+ℓ/R)|^s≤(1−n^(−1/10))Q^(1−γ) for 1≤j<n and all QR=P,Q>1,ℓ. Then Δ_ℙ(n;γn/s+n^0.88)=O_r(exp(−n^(1/10))).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Residue anticoncentration implies a Fourier gap
items.statement: Let P≥2 and η>0. If a probability μ on ℤ has mass≤1−η in every residue class modulo every prime dividing P, then |μhat(k/P)|≤1−4η/P² for P∤k.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Fourier control bounds residue masses
items.statement: If p≥2 prime, s≥1 and Σ_{k mod p}|μhat(k/p)|^s≤p^(1−γ) with γ≥1/2, then every residue mass modulo p is≤p^(−γ/s)≤2^(−1/(2s))≤1−1/(4s).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Small irreducible factors are rare
items.statement: For support μ_j⊂[−exp(n^(1/3)),exp(n^(1/3))], ||μ_j||∞≤1−n^(−1/10) for 1≤j<n, and μ_0 not concentrated at 0, conditional probability given a_0≠0 of an irreducible factor of degree≤n^(1/10) is O(n^(−7/20)), with absolute constant.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Four-prime irreducibility criterion
items.statement: Let ε∈(0,1/100], θ∈(0,1/2], λ0=1/(4−4log2). Assume coefficient supports in ±exp(n^(1/3)); four distinct primes ℙ; Δ_ℙ(n;θn+n^(λ0+ε))≤n^(−30); and, for 1≤j<n, ||μ_j||∞≤1−n^(−1/10), Σ_{a≡0 mod p}μ_j(a)≤1−n^(−ε/200) for every p∈ℙ. Then P(Bad_{θn}(A) AND a_0≠0)≤C(ε)n^(−c(ε)) for some positive C,c depending only on ε.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Master small-factor theorem, corrected event
items.statement: Assume every support lies in ±exp(n^(1/3)), μ_0≠δ_0, P≤n^(1/4) is a product of four distinct primes, γ≥1/2 and integer 1≤s≤n^(1/20000)/4. Assume the Fourier inequality in item 24 for all 1≤j<n. Put θ=γ/s. Then P(Bad_{θn}(A)|a_0≠0)≤C_1 n^(−c) for absolute c,C_1>0. Equivalently, absence of such nonconstant divisors has probability at least 1−C_1n^(−c).
items.locator: arXiv v3, Theorem 7 pp. 13–14, corrected E1
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: One-prime large-Galois criterion
items.statement: For ε>0, a prime p and coefficient laws, assume Δ_p(n;n/2+n^(λ0+ε))≤n^(−10) and every μ_j,1≤j<n, has mass≤1−1/(log n)² in the zero residue class mod p. Then P(A irreducible AND G_A∉{A_n,S_n})≤C(ε)n^(−c(ε)). This is an unconditional joint probability, not P(bad Galois|irreducible).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Four-prime Galois master theorem, corrected hypothesis
items.statement: Assume supports in ±exp(n^(1/3)); P≤n^(1/4) is the product of four distinct primes; and Σ_{k mod Q}|μhat_j(k/Q+ℓ/R)|≤(1−n^(−1/10))Q^(1/2) for 0≤j<n and all QR=P,Q>1,ℓ. Then P(G_A∈{A_n,S_n}|a_0≠0)=1−O(n^(−c)) for an absolute c>0.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Theorem 8 p. 16, corrected E2
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Consecutive intervals of size at least 35
items.statement: There exist absolute c>0,n0 such that, for H≥1, an N-element interval of consecutive integers Nset⊂[−H,H], N≥35, and n≥max(n0,(log H)^3), a uniform A∈Υ_Nset(n) is irreducible with probability≥1−n^(−c).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Short consecutive intervals have positive irreducibility probability
items.statement: There exist absolute δ>0,n0 such that, for H≥1, a consecutive interval Nset⊂[−H,H] with 2≤N≤34 and n≥max(n0,(log H)^3), a uniform A∈Υ_Nset(n) is irreducible with probability≥δ.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: General finite laws: verified weaker quantitative parameter
items.statement: For integers H,n≥3 and iid μ supported on [−H,H] with ||μ||∞≤1−ε, 0<ε<1, there exist absolute c,C,c′>0 such that, when n≥C ε^(−20000)(log H)^(1000000), all nonconstant divisors have degree≥θn with conditional probability≥1−n^(−c), where the argument verified here supplies θ=c′ε/(log H)^9. The source's stronger exponent 5 remains an unresolved target, not an established correction.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Theorem 2 p. 3 and §3.5 p. 25; E4
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Sparse-support l2 criterion
items.statement: For iid μ on ℤ, integers H,n≥3, supp μ⊂[−H,H] and ||μ||_2²≤min(H^(−4/5),n^(1/16)/H)/(log H)^2, there are absolute c>0,H0≥3 such that H≥H0 implies P(A irreducible|a_0≠0)≥1−n^(−c).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Arbitrary finite sets: small-factor exclusion
items.statement: There are absolute c>0,n0≥3 and θ(H)>0 such that for integers H,n≥3, any Nset⊂[−H,H] with N≥2, and n≥max(n0,(log H)^3), a uniform A∈Υ_Nset(n) has every nonconstant divisor of degree≥θ(H)n with probability≥1−n^(−c).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Large arbitrary finite sets: irreducibility
items.statement: For absolute c>0,H0≥3, integers H,n≥3, Nset⊂[−H,H] with N≥H^(4/5)(log H)^2, H≥H0 and n≥(H/N)^16(log H)^32, a uniform A∈Υ_Nset(n) is irreducible with probability≥1−n^(−c).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Odd-power coefficient sets
items.statement: For every positive odd integer d there exist H0(d),n0(d)≥3 and an absolute c>0 such that H≥H0(d), n≥max(n0(d),(log H)^3), and uniform A∈Υ_{ {k^d:1≤k≤H} }(n) imply irreducibility probability≥1−n^(−c).
items.note: Positive d and integer coefficient model are explicit; negative odd exponents do not define the stated integer family.

items.name: A random coefficient set is usually good
items.statement: For H≥1 and integer 2≤N≤|[−H,H]∩ℤ|, choose Nset uniformly among N-element subsets of [−H,H]∩ℤ. There are absolute c>0,n0≥1 such that, with set-probability at least 1−O(N^(−1/2)), for every n≥max(n0,(log H)^3) the conditional uniform polynomial law on Υ_Nset(n) has irreducibility probability≥1−n^(−c).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Alternating or symmetric groups with high probability
items.statement: In the coefficient regimes of items 32,35,38,39, the Galois action of A on its n roots, conditioned on a_0≠0, is A_n or S_n with probability≥1−n^(−c) for an absolute c>0. For item 39 the assertion is inside the same good-set event.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Theorem 6 first part p. 5; §3.7 p. 28
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Alternating or symmetric groups for short intervals
items.statement: In the setting of item 33, the Galois action is A_n or S_n with probability≥δ−n^(−c), after decreasing the absolute δ,c if needed.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Theorem 6 second part p. 5; §3.7 p. 28
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: k-fold irreducibility
items.statement: For a separable degree-n polynomial A∈ℚ[T] and 1≤k≤n, say it is k-fold irreducible when A is irreducible and, for every 1≤j<k, deleting j distinct roots leaves a polynomial irreducible over the field generated by those roots. Multiplication by the leading-coefficient unit does not affect irreducibility.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.42.api1
api.statement: Build the tower of fields generated by an ordered injective root tuple.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.42.api2
api.statement: Deleting roots is division by the corresponding linear factors.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.42.api3
api.statement: Prove independence of the initial root ordering via Galois transport.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: k-fold irreducibility and multiple transitivity
items.statement: For separable A∈ℚ[T] of degree n and 1≤k≤n, k-fold irreducibility is equivalent to k-transitivity of its Galois action on the roots.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: High-order irreducibility, corrected scope
items.statement: In the regimes of Theorems 1(a),3,4,5 (items 32,35,38,39), for n≥3 the random polynomial is (n−2)-fold irreducible with probability≥1−n^(−c). This extraction does not include the general-law regime of Theorem 2.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Corollary 2 p. 5, corrected E3
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Positive-probability high-order irreducibility
items.statement: For n≥3 in the short-interval setting of Theorem 1(b), (n−2)-fold irreducibility has probability≥δ−n^(−c).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Exact Fourier spectrum of a consecutive interval
items.statement: For μ uniform on {a,…,a+N−1}, P≥2 and 1≤k<P, |μhat(k/P)|=|sin(πNk/P)|/(N sin(πk/P)); μhat(0)=1. If N≡r mod P, the numerator depends only on r and k.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Exact certificate for all N≥35
items.statement: For μ uniform on any consecutive N integers with N≥35, α(210)^2<997/1000<1. It suffices to verify the finite set N=35,…,244 because, within each residue class mod 210, every nonzero-frequency modulus in item 46 decreases with N and the zero-frequency term stays 1.
items.locator: arXiv v3, §3.1 pp. 17–18; extraction certificate C1
items.note: A proved finite-reduction argument plus executed exact-rational certificate; not a Lean theorem. Complete executable certificate is embedded in the report.

items.name: Large interval, small degree
items.statement: If Nset is an interval of N consecutive integers contained in [−N^(loglog(100N)),N^(loglog(100N))], and n≤N^(1/200), then the reducible proportion of Υ_Nset(n) is O(N^(−3/10)), with absolute implied constant.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Medium-factor exclusion using an exactly uniform prime
items.statement: For an N-element arithmetic progression Nset of step d, N≥2, a prime p|N with p∤d, and θ∈[0,1/2], the proportion of Υ_Nset(n) with no nonconstant divisor of degree in [θn,n/2] is at least−log(1−θ)+O(1/n), with an absolute implied constant.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Medium-factor exclusion for any progression
items.statement: For an N-element arithmetic progression Nset⊂[−H,H] with N≥2 and θ∈[0,1/2], the proportion of Υ_Nset(n) without a divisor of degree in [θn,n/2] is at least−log(1−θ)−O(log(nH)/(sqrt(n)log N)).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Evaluation bound for an irreducible integral factor
items.statement: If A∈ℤ[T] has degree n, all coefficients bounded by H≥1, and an irreducible monic factor I of degree m divides A, then for integer N≥2, |I(N)|≤N^m exp(4(1+sqrt(m))log(14sqrt(n)H)).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Positive irreducibility for arbitrary arithmetic progressions
items.statement: Let Nset⊂[−H,H] be an N-element arithmetic progression of step d≥1 with N≥2. Let P be the product of the four smallest primes not dividing d. There exist δ(P)>0,n0(P) such that n≥max(n0(P),(log H)^3) implies a uniform A∈Υ_Nset(n) is irreducible with probability≥δ(P). For Nset={−1,1} one can take P=1155, s=735, any γ slightly below γ(735)=0.5000197007327… (/132) and δ=0.00068053.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Random-set Fourier second moment
items.statement: For a uniform N-element subset S of {−H,…,H}, H∈ℕ,N≤2H+1, and θ=k/210 with 1≤k≤209, let δ1=N/(2H+1),δ2=N(N−1)/(2H(2H+1)). Then E|Σ_{a∈S}e(aθ)|²=δ2|Σ_{a=−H}^H e(aθ)|²+(δ1−δ2)(2H+1)=O(N). Consequently EΣ_{k=1}^{209}|μhat_S(k/210)|=O(N^(−1/2)).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Four-prime average from the large sieve
items.statement: For x≥2,H≥1 and μ supported on [−H,H], let N_4(x) be the products of four distinct primes in [x/2,x]. Then Σ_{P∈N_4(x)}α(P)≪(x/log x)^4·((xlogx)^2+sqrt(Hlogx/x))·||μ||_2, with an absolute constant.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Prime-number input
items.statement: π(x)~x/log x as x→∞; hence for x sufficiently large, (x,3x] contains between 4+x/log x and 3x/log x primes, and |N_m(x)|~(x/log x)^m/(m!2^m) for each fixed m.
items.note: Reviewed AUDIT-06 says PNT absent at the pins; Dirichlet infinitude alone is insufficient. The original proof input remains S6.

items.name: Additive large-sieve input
items.statement: For μ supported on integer [−H,H] and y≥1, Σ_{q≤y}Σ_{a mod q,(a,q)=1}|μhat(a/q)|²≪(y²+H)||μ||_2², with absolute implied constant.
items.note: Reviewed AUDIT-07 reports the additive large sieve absent; generic character orthogonality is not this estimate.

items.name: Primes in a coprime progression
items.statement: For q>0 and gcd(a,q)=1, and every bound B, there exists a prime p>B with p≡a mod q. For positive odd d, a=2,q=d permits four distinct such primes; d=1 can be handled directly.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Stronger Mignotte input for factor l2 norms
items.statement: For an integer polynomial A of degree n and an irreducible integer factor I of degree m, the source uses ||I||_2≤exp(sqrt(m))·(m+2sqrt(m)+2)^(1+sqrt(m))·||A||_2^(1+sqrt(m)). Here ||·||_2 is the Euclidean norm of the full coefficient vector. This is the exact inequality displayed in BKK23; its hypotheses and proof in Mignotte 1988 remain a source gate.
items.note: BKK23 p. 20 attributes this to Mignotte 1988 Theorem 1′ and its subsequent remarks. Not the weaker binomial Mignotte bound already in Mathlib. Use ||A||_2≤Hsqrt(n+1), correcting E15.

items.name: Cauchy bounds away from zero
items.statement: For monic integer A of positive degree with all nonleading coefficients |a_j|≤H and a_0≠0, each complex root z satisfies 1/(H+1)<|z|<H+1.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Bounded small-factor coefficient universe
items.statement: If D is a monic degree-m factor of A under item 59, then |coeff_j D|≤binom(m,j)(H+1)^(m−j). For m≤n≤H this is≤(H+1)^m. Consequently the candidate factors of degree≤floor(n^0.1), with H=floor(exp(n^(1/3))), have cardinality≤exp(n^0.54) for all sufficiently large n.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Concentration function
items.statement: For a real random variable X and δ>0, Q(X;δ)=sup_{u∈ℝ}P(|X−u|<δ). This is a real-variable definition; complex sums first require projection as in corrected item 63.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.61.api1
api.statement: Define the supremum over interval centers.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.61.api2
api.statement: An atom of X is bounded by Q(X;δ).

api.name: RandomPolynomial.61.api3
api.statement: Scaling by a nonzero real b gives Q(bX;δ)=Q(X;δ/|b|).

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Kolmogorov–Rogozin input
items.statement: For independent real random variables X_0,…,X_{n−1} and δ>0, Q(ΣX_j;δ)≤C(Σ_j(1−Q(X_j;δ)))^(−1/2), with absolute C, whenever the denominator is positive; otherwise use the trivial bound 1.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lemma 7.2 proof p. 36, citing[19,33,34]
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Root anticoncentration, complex case repaired
items.statement: If ||μ_j||∞≤1−ε for 1≤j<n, n≥2 and ε>0, then for every nonzero complex z, P(A(z)=0)≪1/sqrt(εn), with an absolute constant.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Cyclotomic factor exclusion
items.statement: Under item 63, Σ_{d≥1,φ(d)≤m0}P(Φ_d|A)≪m0/sqrt(εn) for m0≥1, with absolute implied constant.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Inverse-totient counting input
items.statement: For real x≥1, #{d∈ℕ_{>0}:φ(d)≤x}=O(x), with an absolute constant.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lemma 7.3 p. 37, citing Smati[37]
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Mahler measure
items.statement: For f∈ℂ[T], M(0)=0 and for f≠0, M(f)=|lc(f)|∏_{roots w with multiplicity}max(1,|w|). The pinned definition is exp of the circle-average logarithm, with the root formula proved.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.66.api1
api.statement: Use Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, not a parallel definition.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.66.api2
api.statement: M(fg)=M(f)M(g).

api.name: RandomPolynomial.66.api3
api.statement: Map integral polynomials to ℂ before evaluating M.

uses.how: Consumes this exact carrier and its conventions.

items.name: Mahler root formula
items.statement: For every f∈ℂ[T], M(f)=|lc(f)|∏_w max(1,|w|), with roots counted with multiplicity; if f has nonzero integer leading coefficient then M(f)≥∏_w max(1,|w|)≥1.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Mahler coefficient-sum upper bound
items.statement: For f∈ℂ[T], M(f)≤Σ_j|coeff_j f|.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Dobrowolski lower-bound input
items.statement: There exist absolute constants c,C≥1 such that, for a monic irreducible non-cyclotomic D∈ℤ[T], D≠T, of degree m≥1, M(D)≥exp(1/L(m)), where L(m)=2(log m/loglog m)^3 for m>C and L(m)=c for 1≤m≤C. This is Dobrowolski's asymptotic bound M(α)>1+(1−ε)(loglog m/log m)^3 (m≥m_0(ε)); the printed L(m)=(1/2)(log m/loglog m)^3 needs the constant 2 of Cantor–Straus or Louboutin (E21).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Few primes drop algebraic degree
items.statement: For a nonzero algebraic number α of degree m over ℚ, at most log m/log 2 primes p satisfy[ℚ(α^p):ℚ]<m. Consequently, for H=floor(exp(n^(1/3))) and m≤n^0.1, there is for n sufficiently large a prime L(m)log(2Hn)<p≤2L(m)log(2Hn) for which α^p retains degree m.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Sparse coefficient uniqueness
items.statement: Let D be a monic noncyclotomic irreducible integer polynomial with nonzero roots z_i, and let p be a prime such that the z_i^p are distinct and p>L(m)log(2Hn), with M(D)≥exp(1/L(m)). Given all a_j for 0≤j<n with p∤j, at most one monic degree-n A with |a_j|≤H and D|A has those coefficients.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Polynomial sieve datum
items.statement: For finite ℙ, let I_p be a finite set of monic irreducible polynomials in 𝔽_p[T]. Define(A_p,I_p)=∏_{J∈I_p,J|A_p}J, and G|I means G_p divides∏_{J∈I_p}J for every p; thus G_p is squarefree. The probability law on∏M_p(n) can be arbitrary, not a product.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.72.api1
api.statement: Construct the squarefree product of selected irreducibles.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.72.api2
api.statement: (A/D,I)=1 on the event D|A means no selected prime factor remains.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.72.api3
api.statement: Parameterize every squarefree sieve divisor by a subset of I_p.

items.name: Prime-polynomial bounds
items.statement: For a prime p and integer k≥1, if π_p(k) counts monic irreducible degree-k polynomials over 𝔽_p, then (p^k−2p^(k/2))/k≤π_p(k)≤p^k/k. Hence Σ_{deg I=k}1/||I||_p≤1/k.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Squarefree Bonferroni sieve inequality
items.statement: If B is squarefree and v≥1 integer, then Σ_{G|B,ω(G)≤2v−1}(−1)^ω(G)≤1_{B=1}≤Σ_{G|B,ω(G)≤2v}(−1)^ω(G). Here divisors are monic and ω counts distinct irreducible factors.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Brun upper bound for general joint polynomial laws
items.statement: Let ℙ contain r primes and let ν be any law on M_ℙ(n). For monic D_p and selected irreducibles I_p of degrees≤ℓ_p with ℓ_p≥11, ν(D|A,(A/D,I)=1)≤(2^r/||D||)∏_{p,J∈I_p}(1−1/||J||)+Σ_{G|I,ω(G_p)≤6logℓ_p ∀p}|ν(DG|A)−1/||DG|| |. Every G_p in the remainder has degree≤6ℓ_p log ℓ_p.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Small-prime Euler product bound
items.statement: For m≥0 integer and prime p, let I be all monic irreducibles J≠T of degree≤m. Then ∏_{J∈I}(1−1/||J||_p)≤2/(m+1).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Polynomial divisor and prime-factor counts
items.statement: For nonzero A∈𝔽_p[T], τ(A) is the number of monic divisors and ω(A) the number of distinct monic irreducible factors. If A=unit·∏I^ν_I, then τ(A)=∏(ν_I+1), ω(A)=#{I:ν_I>0}, and τ(A)≥2^ω(A), with equality for squarefree A.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.77.api1
api.statement: Define the finite monic-divisor set and distinct-factor support.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.77.api2
api.statement: Prove coprime multiplicativity of τ and additivity of ω.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.77.api3
api.statement: τ(I^ν)=ν+1; ω(I^ν)=1 for ν≥1.

items.name: Smooth and rough parts excluding T
items.statement: For monic A∈𝔽_p[T] and integer m≥0, A^S(m) is the full product of powers of irreducible factors I≠T with deg I≤m; A^R(m)=A/A^S(m). Thus all powers of T belong to the rough part even when m≥1.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.78.api1
api.statement: Construct both parts with A=A^S·A^R and coprime factors.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.78.api2
api.statement: Smooth part is monotone under increasing m in the divisibility order.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.78.api3
api.statement: A factor divides the smooth part iff all its irreducible factors are allowed.

items.name: Additive polynomial functions
items.statement: An additive function f on nonzero 𝔽_p[T] satisfies f(AB)=f(A)+f(B) when gcd(A,B)=1. In Lemma 9.2 it is nonnegative, f(I)∈{0,1} and 0≤f(I^ν)≤C1 log ν for ν≥2,C1≥3.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.79.api1
api.statement: Build f from its values on prime powers; units contribute 0.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.79.api2
api.statement: Evaluate f by summing over distinct irreducible factors with their exponents.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.79.api3
api.statement: Instantiate ω and log τ/log 2, keeping repeated factors.

items.name: Additive-function intensity
items.statement: For f as in item 79 and m≥1, L_f(m)=Σ_{I monic irreducible,deg I≤m,f(I)=1}1/||I||_p. This sum includes T, although A^S(m) excludes T; the difference in the estimates is uniformly bounded.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.80.api1
api.statement: Define the finite intensity sum including the degree-one prime T.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.80.api2
api.statement: L_ω(m)=log m+O(1) from the prime-polynomial bounds.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.80.api3
api.statement: For degree indicator f(I)=g(deg I), compare L_f(m) with Σ_{k≤m}g(k)/k up to O(1).

items.name: Smooth part degree tail
items.statement: Fix C≥1, prime p, integer n≥3, integer 4C≤m≤n and u≥2. For arbitrary independent coefficient laws, P(deg A_p^S(m)>um)≤O_C(m exp(−Cu))+Δ_p(n;um).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Lower tail of an additive function
items.statement: Let θ∈(0,1), C1,C2≥3, f satisfy item 79, and integer 1≤m≤2θn/log n. Uniformly 0≤t≤1, P(f(A_p^S(m))≤tL_f(m))≪exp(−(tlogt−t+1)L_f(m))+n^8Δ_p(n;θn), with 0log0=0.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Upper tail of an additive function
items.statement: Under item 82's hypotheses, uniformly 1≤t≤C2, P(f(A_p^S(m))≥tL_f(m))≪_{C1,C2}exp(−(tlogt−t+1)L_f(m))+n^max(7,t+5)Δ_p(n;θn).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Uniform smooth-part control
items.statement: Let θ,ε∈(0,1), ℙ a set of r primes, and Δ_p(n;θn)≤n^(−8) for every p∈ℙ. There is c=c(ε)>0 such that for every 1≤m0≤2θn/log n, with probability≥1−O_{ε,r}(m0^(−c)), simultaneously all integer m∈[m0,2θn/log n] and p∈ℙ satisfy deg A_p^S(m)≤εm log m and τ(A_p^S(m))≤m^((1+ε)log 2).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Simultaneous degree-k divisors on the good event
items.statement: Let θ∈(0,1/2],δ∈(0,1],λ∈(0,1), ε∈(0,1), r=|ℙ|, n≥2. Suppose Δ_ℙ(n;θn+n^λ)≤n^(−7r) and zero-residue mass of μ_j mod p is≤1−δ for all p and 1≤j<n. For integer 1≤k≤θn let E be the event in item 84 on m∈[k^(λ/2),2θn/log n]. Then P(E AND every A_p has a monic degree-k divisor)≪_{r,ε,λ}(log²n/(δ k^((1−log 2−ε)λ)))^r.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Galois permutation representation
items.statement: For A∈ℚ[T], its splitting-field automorphism group acts faithfully on its distinct roots. Use Polynomial.Gal.galActionHom. For separable degree-n A this root set has cardinality n; a choice of numbering identifies the image with a subgroup of S_n, unique up to conjugacy.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.86.api1
api.statement: Reuse the splitting-field action and its injectivity.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.86.api2
api.statement: Transport the image along any root numbering.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.86.api3
api.statement: Conjugacy-invariant statements do not depend on the numbering.

items.name: Transitivity versus irreducibility with separability
items.statement: For separable positive-degree A over a field, in a splitting extension E, its Galois action on rootSet A E is transitive iff A is irreducible. For characteristic-zero irreducible A, separability is automatic. The reverse implication without separability is false.
items.locator: arXiv v3, §1 p. 4; §11 p. 54, qualified E16
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Full cycle type
items.statement: The cycle type used in the paper is the partition of n consisting of ALL cycle lengths, including fixed points. Use Equiv.Perm.partition or Tau Ceti's fullCycleType=cycleType+replicate(n−support.card,1), not Mathlib's cycleType alone.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.88.api1
api.statement: Use the existing full-cycle multiset and its partition proof.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.88.api2
api.statement: The sum of parts is n and the number of 1s is the fixed-point count.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.88.api3
api.statement: Conjugation and relabelling preserve full cycle type.

items.name: Factorization partition with multiplicity
items.statement: For monic integral A of degree n and prime p, τ_{A_p} is the multiset of degrees of irreducible factors of A mod p counted WITH multiplicity, summing to n. Use Polynomial.factorDegrees; equal degrees from different factors and repeated copies are both retained.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.89.api1
api.statement: Reuse Polynomial.factorDegrees on the integral lift.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.89.api2
api.statement: Use Monic.sum_factorDegrees to construct the partition of n.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.89.api3
api.statement: A singleton{n} is equivalent to irreducibility of A mod p.

items.name: Induced partition law
items.statement: For A∼PM(n) and prime p, ν is the pushforward measure on partitions of n under A↦τ_{A_p}. Thus ν(E)=P(τ_{A_p}∈E); it is not assumed to be the partition law of a uniform permutation.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.90.api1
api.statement: Push the polynomial law along its factor-degree partition.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.90.api2
api.statement: Express submultiset events as factor-degree events.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.90.api3
api.statement: Transport integrals and event probabilities by the pushforward identity.

items.name: Union of bad transitive subgroups
items.statement: For n≥1, T_n is the subset of S_n formed by the union of all transitive subgroups other than A_n and S_n. It is a set of permutations, not itself a subgroup in general.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.91.api1
api.statement: Membership includes a witness transitive subgroup G≠A_n,S_n.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.91.api2
api.statement: T_n is closed under conjugation as a set.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.91.api3
api.statement: For a bad transitive G, every element lies in T_n; the converse containment needs care.

items.name: Bounded merging of equal partition parts
items.statement: For partitions ρ=(ρ_1,…,ρ_r) and σ of n and y≥1, σ is a y-merging of ρ if the index set [r] partitions into nonempty blocks B_i, each |B_i|≤y, all ρ_j in each B_i equal, and σ_i=Σ_{j∈B_i}ρ_j. Merge(ρ;y) is the set of permutations with full cycle type such aσ.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.92.api1
api.statement: Construct merging from a partition of part INDICES, not values.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.92.api2
api.statement: Identity merging exists for every y≥1; composition multiplies the bound.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.92.api3
api.statement: Merge is monotone in y and invariant under reorderingρ and conjugating permutations.

items.name: Maximum irreducible multiplicity
items.statement: For monic positive-degree A_p, M(A_p)=max_I v_I(A_p), over monic irreducible factors. Each root of an irreducible factor I of exponent m has exactly m lifts among the n distinct characteristic-zero roots, counted as reduction fibers.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.93.api1
api.statement: Take the maximum of the finite positive multiplicities.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.93.api2
api.statement: A squarefree reduction has M=1.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.93.api3
api.statement: Bound every reduction fiber by M without assuming unramified reduction.

items.name: Partition pair bound
items.statement: Assume n≥16,0<λ<1, Δ_p(n;n/2+n^λ)≤n^(−10), and zero-residue mass≤1−1/(log n)² for 1≤j<n. For integers 2≤k,ℓ≤n/4, ν({k,ℓ}⊂ρ)≤2/(kℓ), interpreting repeated parts with multiplicity.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Partition subset-sum bound
items.statement: Under item 94's hypotheses, there is absolute c>0 such that for every integer n^(1/10)≤k≤n/2, ν(∃submultisetU⊂ρ,ΣU=k)≪_λ k^(−cλ).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Partition lower-tail bound
items.statement: Under item 94's hypotheses, for f:ℕ→{0,1}, integer 1≤m≤n/log n,t∈(0,1), and L=Σ_{k≤m}f(k)/k, one has ν(Σ_{k∈ρ,k≤m}f(k)≤tL)≪exp(−(tlogt−t+1)L), summing parts with multiplicity.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Arithmetic Frobenius lift at a possibly ramified prime
items.statement: For a finite Galois number field F/ℚ and a prime ideal Q⊂O_F above the rational prime p, there exists σ∈Gal(F/ℚ) with σ(x)≡x^p mod Q for every x∈O_F. No unramified hypothesis is required for existence; uniqueness is not asserted.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Finite-field Frobenius orbits of a factor
items.statement: For a polynomial g over a finite field F and an algebraic splitting extension E, every monic irreducible factor q of g has a root whose orbit under x↦x^|F| is exactly q.rootSet E and has cardinality deg q.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Orbit lengths over a cyclic reduction orbit
items.statement: Let a permutation φ of a finite set cyclically permute d disjoint fibers of common size m. Every φ-orbit in their union has size d·m′ for some integer 1≤m′≤m; its intersections with each fiber have the same m′ elements.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Ramified factorization gives a merging cycle type
items.statement: For monic squarefree A∈ℤ[T] of degree n≥1, a prime p and M=max_Iv_I(A mod p), the Galois group of A contains an element whose full cycle type is an M-merging of τ_{A_p}.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Large repeated factors have small probability
items.statement: For n sufficiently large, assume Δ_p(n;n/log n)≤1/n and zero-residue mass≤1−1/(log n)² for every 1≤j<n. Then the probability that some monic irreducible I divides A_p to exponent>(log n)^3 is O(1/n). The source states the stronger premise also at j=0; this weakening follows from its proof and is needed by Proposition 2.4.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Polylogarithmic mergings avoid bad transitive groups
items.statement: Under item 94's hypotheses there is absolute c>0 such that ν(∃g∈T_n with full cycle type a(log n)^3-merging of ρ)≪_λ n^(−cλ).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Generalized Łuczak–Pyber theorem
items.statement: Let ν be any probability on partitions of n. Suppose C≥1,t∈(0,1),κ∈(0,1],δ∈(0,1/10] and: (a)ν({k,ℓ}⊂ρ)≤C/(kℓ) for 2≤k,ℓ≤n/4; (b)ν(∃U⊂ρ,ΣU=k)≤Ck^(−δ) for n^(1−δ/2)≤k≤n/2; (c)for every f:ℕ→{0,1},m≤n/log n,L=Σ_{k≤m}f(k)/k,ν(Σ_{k∈ρ,k≤m}f(k)≤tL)≤Cexp(−κL). For fixed ε∈(0,δ/2), the claimed conclusion is ν(Merge(ρ;n^θ)∩T_n≠∅)≪_{C,t,κ,δ,ε}(log n)^2 n^(−κ(δ/4−θ/2)), uniformly 0≤θ≤δ/2−ε. Acceptance requires the missing large-part argument in E12; the corrected extraction treats this as a gated target.
items.note: No unconditional completed proof is asserted in this checkpoint.

items.name: Small-pair gcd event E1
items.statement: With Proposition 12.1 parameters and α=δ/4−θ/2∈[ε/2,1/40], E1 consists of partitions ρ with no two parts k,ℓ≤n/4, counted with multiplicity, satisfying gcd(k,ℓ)≥n^(κα). There is NO restriction on a pair involving a part>n/4.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.104.api1
api.statement: Define the event through pairs of distinct part indices.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.104.api2
api.statement: If ρ∈E1, every k∈[n^(κα),n/4] occurs at most once.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.104.api3
api.statement: Expose k,ℓ≤n/4 whenever using the gcd bound.

items.name: Block-fraction subset-sum event E2
items.statement: E2 consists of partitions ρ with no submultiset sum nj/r for any divisor r|n with 2≤r≤n^(δ/2) and 1≤j<r.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.105.api1
api.statement: Enumerate admissible divisorsr and proper indicesj.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.105.api2
api.statement: A forbidden subset has a complementary forbidden subset, so restrictj≤r/2.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.105.api3
api.statement: Transport a union of block-orbits to its subset of partition parts.

items.name: Many large parts event E3
items.statement: E3 means that ρ has at least (αt/2)log n parts, counted with multiplicity, in [n^(1−α),n/log n], with α as in item 104.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.106.api1
api.statement: Count the interval-filtered multiset.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.106.api2
api.statement: For n sufficiently large this provides at least any prescribed fixed number of parts.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.106.api3
api.statement: Under E1 these parts are distinct for large n.

items.name: Large-prime small parts event E4
items.statement: E4 means that ρ has at least (t/4)log n parts, with multiplicity, satisfying k≤sqrt(n)/3 and divisible by some prime p>n^(1/8).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.107.api1
api.statement: Define the filter by existence of a sufficiently large prime divisor.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.107.api2
api.statement: Every selected part is>n^(1/8).

api.name: RandomPolynomial.107.api3
api.statement: E1 makes selected parts distinct for sufficiently large n.

items.name: Large parts not divisible by r event E5 (strengthened)
items.statement: E5 consists of the partitions ρ such that for every integer r≥2 at least four parts k∈ρ∩[n^(1−2α),n/log n], counted with multiplicity, satisfy r∤k. The source's E5 asks for one such part; Case 3 of Lemma 12.9 needs four (E12).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.108.api1
api.statement: Define the universal nondivisibility event.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.108.api2
api.statement: Under E1∩E3 only r≤n^(κα) need probabilistic estimates.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.108.api3
api.statement: For each r, use the degree indicator 1_{k≥n^(1−2α),r∤k}.

items.name: Pair gcd failure probability
items.statement: If ν satisfies Proposition 12.1(a), then P(E1)≥1−O((log n)^2 n^(−κα)), with parameters and asymptotic regime as in item 103.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Block-fraction failure probability
items.statement: If ν satisfies Proposition 12.1(b), then P(E2)≥1−O(n^(−δ/4)).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Many-large-parts probability
items.statement: If ν satisfies Proposition 12.1(c), then P(E3)≥1−O((log n)^κ n^(−κα)).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Large-prime small-parts probability
items.statement: If ν satisfies Proposition 12.1(c), then P(E4)≥1−O(n^(−κ/4)).
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Nondivisibility event probability
items.statement: If ν satisfies Proposition 12.1(a),(c), then P(E5)≥1−O((log n)^2 n^(−κα)), for E5 as in /108.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Minimum permutation degree
items.statement: For g∈S_n, deg g=|{i:g(i)≠i}|. For a nontrivial subgroup G≤S_n, mindegG=min_{g∈G,g≠1}deg g. Nontriviality is required for this minimum rather than silently assigning a value for an empty set.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.114.api1
api.statement: Use the existing finite support of a permutation.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.114.api2
api.statement: Define mindeg with a nonidentity witness.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.114.api3
api.statement: Any nonidentity power g^m∈G gives an upper bound mindegG≤deg(g^m).

items.name: Primitive-group minimum-degree bound
items.statement: If G≤S_n is transitive and primitive, G≠A_n,S_n, then mindegG≥(sqrt(n)−1)/2, in the nontrivial range of the statement.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lemma 12.7, p. 62, citing Bary-Soroker–Kozma 2020 Claim 1
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Primitive-group exclusion for typical partitions
items.statement: For n sufficiently large in the fixed Proposition 12.1 parameters, if ρ∈E1∩E4 and g∈Merge(ρ;n^(1/8)), then g belongs to no primitive transitive subgroup other than A_n,S_n.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Imprimitive-group exclusion
items.statement: For n≥n_0, 0≤θ≤δ/2−ε and ρ∈E1∩…∩E5 (E5 as in /108), no g∈Merge(ρ;n^θ) lies in a transitive imprimitive subgroup of S_n.
items.note: The printed proof applies E1 to a companion part k that may exceed n/4 (E12). The proof steps above are this continuation's repair; they use only E1, E3 and the strengthened E5, and the lemma's statement is unchanged.

items.name: Scalar Chinese remainder equivalence
items.statement: For coprime positive integers m,n, ℤ/(mn)≃ℤ/m×ℤ/n as rings. Iteration over distinct primes identifies ℤ/P with∏𝔽_p.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Finite additive-character orthogonality
items.statement: For a finite additive group G and a complex-valued additive character ψ, Σ_{x∈G}ψ(x)=|G| if ψ is trivial and 0 otherwise.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Basic factor coefficient bound already present
items.statement: For complex polynomials g,h with M(h)≥1 and n≥0, |coeff_n(g)|≤binom(deg g,n)M(gh). This specializes to nonzero integral cofactors, but does not imply the sharper sqrt(deg g) l2 estimate used in Lemma 3.4.
items.locator: arXiv v3, §7 coefficient bounds; comparison for Lemma 3.4
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Landau l2 bound already present
items.statement: For every complex polynomial f, M(f)≤sqrt(Σ_j|coeff_j f|²), with the sum over its finite support.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Mahler input comparison for §§3.3,7
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Polynomial-value Fourier estimate with repaired hypotheses
items.statement: Let f∈ℤ[T] have degree d≥1. Let μ be the PUSHFORWARD of uniform {1,…,N} by f, not necessarily uniform on its image. If Q is squarefree and f mod p is nonconstant for every p|Q, then for any realshiftβ, Σ_{k mod Q}|μhat(k/Q+β)|²≤d^ω(Q)(1+Q/N). If f is injective on {1,…,N}, this also holds for the uniform image-set law. The source's closing bound d^ω(Q)(1+Q/N)≤Q^ε/2 (for N≥Q and prime factors of Q at least d^(4/ε)) needs d≥2.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Remark 3.2 p. 23, corrected E13
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Square-coefficient irreducibility extension: source sketch only
items.statement: Remark 3.2 claims that, for Nset={k²:1≤k≤N}, the reducible proportion of Υ_Nset(n) tends to 0 as both N,n→∞. The sketch combines the near-half small-factor criterion with a uniform short-window divisor bound over 𝔽_2; the latter estimate and its two-parameter limiting ranges must be supplied before this becomes an accepted theorem item.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Optimal Fourier exponents
items.statement: For finitely many coefficient laws, squarefree P>1 and s≥1, define γ(s)∈[0,1] uniquely by max_{j,QR=P,Q>1,0≤ℓ<R} Q^(γ(s)−1) Σ_{k=0}^{Q−1}|μhat_j(k/Q+ℓ/R)|^s=1. Set θ(s)=γ(s)/s. Include every coefficient index used by the intended criterion.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.124.api1
api.statement: Existence and uniqueness follow from continuity and strict increase of the finite maximum in γ; at γ=0 it is≤1 and at γ=1 the zero-frequency coset is≥1. If expressing γ as a minimum of logarithms, omit zero moment sums.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.124.api2
api.statement: Expose dependence on the coefficient index range, including j=0 when used here.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.124.api3
api.statement: Recover θ(s) as γ(s)/s with s>0.

items.name: Corrected monotonicity and Hölder concavity of optimal exponents
items.statement: For 1≤s≤t, γ(s)≤γ(t) and θ(s)≥θ(t). For a,b≥1 and 0≤λ≤1, γ(λa+(1−λ)b)≥λγ(a)+(1−λ)γ(b). The displayed comparison γ(s)≥γ(us)/u+γ(vs)/v in Remark 2.2 is false; it is not a target.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Four-prime summability threshold
items.statement: λ0=1/(4−4log2)∈(0.8,0.82). It is characterized by 4(1−log 2)λ0=1 and measures the degree surplus needed to sum the four simultaneous divisor probabilities.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.126.api1
api.statement: Define λ0 with proof that the denominator is positive.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.126.api2
api.statement: Prove 4(1−log 2)λ0=1.

items.name: Products of distinct medium primes
items.statement: For x≥2 and integer m≥0, N_m(x) is the set of products of m DISTINCT primes in [x/2,x], with N_0(x)={1}. Products correspond to unordered subsets, not ordered tuples.
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.127.api1
api.statement: Construct the finite set from m-element subsets of interval primes.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.127.api2
api.statement: Every P∈N_m(x) satisfies(x/2)^m≤P≤x^m.

api.name: RandomPolynomial.127.api3
api.statement: Unique prime factorization gives cardinality binom(number of interval primes,m).

items.name: Mertens sum and product inputs
items.statement: For x≥2, Σ_{p≤x}1/p=loglog x+B+O(1/log x), and ∏_{p≤x}(1−1/p)^(−1)=e^γ log x+O(1), with absolute constants. Each p is a positive rational prime and γ is Euler's constant.
items.locator: arXiv v3, §3.3 p. 21 and §12.1 pp. 60–61, citing[22] Theorem 3.4(b,c)
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Subpower divisor bound
items.statement: For every η>0 there is C_η such that the number τ(k) of positive divisors of each integer k≥1 is≤C_η k^η.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lemma 3.1 pp. 17–18 and Lemma 12.3 p. 60
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Prime polynomials with prescribed nonzero constant
items.statement: For prime p, integer r≥1 and b∈𝔽_p^×, the number of monic irreducible degree-r polynomials with constant coefficient b is p^r/((p−1)r)·(1+O(p^(1−r/2))), with an absolute implied constant.
items.locator: arXiv v3, Lemma 3.2 proof p. 20, invoking Rosen[35] Theorem 4.8
items.note: Not a claim of formalization. See sourceIssues and the report.

items.name: Small-factor exclusion for supports up to exp(Cn^(1/3))
items.statement: Fix C ≥ 1. Let μ_0,…,μ_{n−1} be probability measures on ℤ with supp(μ_j) ⊆ [−exp(Cn^(1/3)), exp(Cn^(1/3))] for all j, ‖μ_j‖_∞ ≤ 1−n^(−1/10) for 1 ≤ j < n, and supp(μ_0) ≠ {0}. Then, for n ≥ n_0(C), P_{M(n)}(A has an irreducible factor of degree ≤ n^(1/10) | a_0 ≠ 0) ≪ n^(−7/20). Consequently Theorems 7 and 8 (/29, /31) hold with condition (a) replaced by the support bound exp(Cn^(1/3)), with n_0 depending on C.
items.locator: §7, pp. 35–38 (the proof of Proposition 2.1, run with H = ⌊exp(Cn^(1/3))⌋); needed for Theorem 4, §3.3, p. 23 (E18)
items.note: Worker repair of E18 in this continuation, not a statement of the paper. With C = d it gives Theorem 4 (/38) in the printed range n ≥ max(n_0(d),(log H)^3).

items.name: Fourier exponent certificates for Theorem 1(b) and for coefficients ±1
items.locator: §3.2, Table 1, p. 19; proof of Theorem 3.5, p. 22 (E20)
items.note: A numerical certificate, not an exact-rational one like /47. The printed γ column rounds γ(s_N) to the nearest unit in the last place, so 15 printed values exceed γ(s_N) (E20); any γ below γ(s_N) works.

items.name: Large Galois group for arithmetic-progression coefficients
items.statement: Let 𝒩 ⊂ [−H,H] be an arithmetic progression of step d with N ≥ 2 elements, and suppose some prime p divides N but not d. With P, δ = δ(P) and n_0(P) as in Theorem 3.5 (/52), for n ≥ max(n_0,(log H)^3) a uniformly random A ∈ Υ_𝒩(n) has Galois group A_n or S_n with probability ≥ δ − n^(−c), for an absolute c > 0.
items.note: The paper states this in Remark 3.3 without a separate proof and notes that it does not cover 𝒩 = {−1, 1}.
